scenarios.depth_note: Tests deemed filing and early-claim reduction: spouse claiming at 62 gets reduced spousal benefit and is deemed to file for own benefit too.
scenarios.prompt: My wife is 62, barely worked so her own benefit is tiny. I'm 66 and just filed for my $2,850/month. Can she get spousal benefits on my record now, and how much would she actually get?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests that spousal benefit maxes at 50% of worker's PIA and delayed retirement credits do NOT increase the spousal amount.
scenarios.prompt: I delayed to 70 so my check is $3,920/month. My wife is 68 and took her own benefit early at 62 ($1,100/month). Does she get a spousal top-up on my record, and do my delayed credits boost it?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests 10-year marriage rule, independent entitlement without affecting ex's benefit, and no consent/notification requirement.
scenarios.prompt: I divorced 6 years ago after a 14-year marriage. I'm 64, my ex-husband is 66 and already collecting. Can I claim on his record? Does it reduce his check, and do I need his permission?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests remarriage termination of divorcee benefits vs the age-60 survivor remarriage exception when widowed from second marriage.
scenarios.prompt: I divorced my first husband after 12 years, remarried at 58, and now at 63 I'm widowed from my second husband. Can I claim a survivor benefit, a divorcee benefit off my first husband, or do I have to pick? Which pays more?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests present-value comparison of lump sum vs annuity: discount rates, mortality credits, and breakeven life expectancy math.
scenarios.prompt: My old employer offered me $184,000 cash now or $1,150/month for life starting at 65. I'm 58. Which is actually the better deal? Show me the math.

scenarios.depth_note: Tests health-adjusted life expectancy: personal mortality info flips the standard annuity-vs-lump-sum analysis.
scenarios.prompt: Buyout offer expires in 45 days: $96,000 lump sum or $620/month at 65. I'm 61 with heart issues and my dad died at 68. How should my health change this decision?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests understanding of cash-balance conversions: pay credits vs old final-average formula, wear-away periods, and who wins/loses.
scenarios.prompt: My company froze the old pension and moved me to a cash-balance plan: 4% pay credits plus 3% interest credits. I'm 45 with 18 years in. Am I getting screwed compared to the old formula?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests lump-sum vs in-plan decision at separation: interest crediting rate vs expected market returns, rollover to IRA option.
scenarios.prompt: I'm leaving my job at 52 with a $142,000 cash-balance account. Should I take the lump sum, roll it into an IRA, or leave it in the plan to keep growing at their interest crediting rate?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests mega backdoor Roth mechanics: total 415(c) limit, and the plan must allow in-service distributions or in-plan Roth conversions.
scenarios.prompt: My 401k allows after-tax contributions up to the $70,000 total limit. I already do $23,500 pre-tax plus a $9,000 employer match. Can I stuff in another $37,500 after-tax and immediately convert it to Roth?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests when after-tax contributions WITHOUT conversion rights are a bad deal vs taxable brokerage (pro-rata earnings taxation).
scenarios.prompt: I put $18,000 into after-tax 401k contributions, but my plan won't allow in-service Roth conversions until I'm 59 and a half. Is that after-tax money still worth it, or would a regular brokerage account be better?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests lifecycle bracket arbitrage for a young worker: current marginal rate vs expected retirement rate; employer match is always pre-tax.
scenarios.prompt: I'm 28 making $92,000 (22% bracket). My employer matches 4% either way. Should my $23,500 go into Roth or traditional 401k? Everyone at work says Roth because I'm young — are they right?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests forward-looking switching decision at peak earnings: past Roth contributions are sunk, only future contributions matter.
scenarios.prompt: I'm 54, peak earning years at $210,000 in the 32% bracket, retiring at 62 on much less income. I've done Roth 401k for a decade. Should I switch to traditional now?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests that 457b has a SEPARATE contribution limit from 401k/403b and governmental 457b has no 10% early withdrawal penalty.
scenarios.prompt: I work for the state and have access to both a 401k and a 457b. I'm 57. Can I really max both at $23,500 each for $47,000 total? And is there an early withdrawal penalty on the 457b like the 401k?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests the special 3-year 457b catch-up: double limit or limit plus underutilized amounts, only in final 3 years before normal retirement age.
scenarios.prompt: I'm a 50-year-old city firefighter with a 457b. My department offers the 3-year special catch-up. I barely contributed in my 30s. How does the catch-up actually work — do I get double the limit?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests 403b-to-401k rollover eligibility and the shared 402(g) elective deferral limit across both plans in the same year.
scenarios.prompt: I left my nonprofit job (had a 403b) for a private company with a 401k. Can I roll the old 403b into the new 401k? And if I contributed to both this year, do they share one contribution limit?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests the 403b 15-year service catch-up ($3k/yr, $15k lifetime) and its ordering vs the age-50 catch-up.
scenarios.prompt: My hospital 403b offers a 15-year catch-up provision. I've worked there 17 years and I'm 52. Do I qualify for the extra $3,000, and does it stack on top of the age-50 catch-up?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests SIMPLE IRA employer funding mandate: 2% nonelective vs 3% match, required even if employee contributes nothing.
scenarios.prompt: I run a business with 6 employees and want to start a SIMPLE IRA. What do I actually have to contribute as the employer, and what if an employee contributes zero?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests the 100-employee limit and the 2-year grace period when a business outgrows SIMPLE IRA eligibility.
scenarios.prompt: I have a SIMPLE IRA for my small business but we just hired our 105th employee counting part-timers. Do I have to kill the plan immediately?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests SEP contribution math for self-employed: 25% of net adjusted self-employment income (effectively ~20% after the SE tax deduction).
scenarios.prompt: I'm self-employed with $180,000 net profit. What's the max I can put in a SEP IRA? Is it really 25% of the full $180k, or is the math trickier than that?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests SEP + 401k coordination: SEP employer contributions don't count against the 402(g) elective deferral limit but share the 415(c) limit per employer.
scenarios.prompt: I have a SEP IRA from freelance work and just took a W-2 job with a 401k. Can I still contribute to the SEP this year, and do the two plans' limits interfere with each other?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests Solo 401k loan rules: lesser of 50% or $50k, 5-year max term, quarterly payments, plan document must allow loans.
scenarios.prompt: My Solo 401k has $210,000 in it and I need $40,000 for a business emergency. Can I borrow from my own Solo 401k? What are the repayment rules?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests loan offset on plan termination: outstanding loan becomes a deemed distribution with a rollover window to avoid taxes.
scenarios.prompt: I took a $35,000 loan from my Solo 401k last year and now I'm shutting down the business entirely. What happens to the loan — do I owe it all back immediately?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests first-RMD timing (April 1 after turning 73), the double-distribution trap, and the uniform lifetime table calculation.
scenarios.prompt: I turn 73 in November 2026 with $890,000 across two traditional IRAs. When is my first RMD actually due, how much is it, and I heard there's a trap if I wait — what is it?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests SECURE Act 10-year rule for non-eligible designated beneficiaries inheriting after 2020, including annual RMDs within the 10 years.
scenarios.prompt: I inherited a traditional IRA from my dad when he died in 2024. I'm 45. Someone told me I have 10 years to empty it — is that the whole story, or do I have to take money out each year too?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests QLAC RMD exclusion: $200k max (SECURE 2.0), excluded from RMD calculation until payments begin, max start age 85.
scenarios.prompt: I'm 68 with $1.2M in a traditional IRA, and RMDs are going to shove me into a higher bracket. Can a QLAC actually shrink my RMDs? What's the most I'm allowed to put in one?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests mortality-credit tradeoff: pure longevity QLAC vs return-of-premium rider, what heirs get if you die before payments start.
scenarios.prompt: I'm looking at a $150,000 QLAC that starts paying at 80. If I die at 78 before a single payment, does my family get anything back or does the insurance company keep it all?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests IRMAA brackets on Parts B and D plus the still-working past 65 rule: creditable employer coverage (20+ employees) avoids late penalties.
scenarios.prompt: I turn 65 in March but I'm still working — my company has 300 employees and good insurance. My income is $130,000 filing single. What will Medicare Parts B and D actually cost me, and do I even need to sign up now?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests IRMAA 2-year lookback on MAGI and which life-changing events qualify for appeal (property sale generally does not).
scenarios.prompt: I'm 72 on Medicare and my Part B premium just jumped $120/month. Last year I sold a rental property for a $200k gain. Is the spike because of that sale, and can I appeal it?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests the one-way door: Medigap guaranteed issue at 65, medical underwriting if you try to switch back later; Advantage network and MOOP tradeoffs.
scenarios.prompt: I'm 65 and healthy. Choice is Medigap Plan G at $185/month or a $0-premium Medicare Advantage plan with a $6,700 max out-of-pocket. What's the real tradeoff nobody tells you about?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests underwriting lock-in: leaving Advantage for Medigap after guaranteed-issue window means health screening and possible denial.
scenarios.prompt: I'm 71 on a Medicare Advantage plan and just got a diagnosis needing a specialist at Mayo Clinic, which is out of network. Can I switch to Medigap now, or am I stuck?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests dollar-for-dollar asset disregard: partnership policy benefits paid = assets shielded from Medicaid spend-down.
scenarios.prompt: My state has a long-term care partnership program. If I buy a $250,000 partnership policy and later need Medicaid, how exactly does that protect my assets? Walk me through the math.

scenarios.depth_note: Tests cost-benefit of partnership premiums vs self-insuring, factoring home equity and total net worth.
scenarios.prompt: I'm 58, quotes for a partnership LTC policy are $3,200/year. My net worth is $900,000 but most of it is home equity. Is the policy worth it, or should I just self-insure?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests current exemption amount, portability between spouses, and urgency of lifetime gifting before law changes.
scenarios.prompt: I heard the estate tax exemption was supposed to get cut in half. What's the actual exemption for 2026? My parents have a $16M estate — should they be gifting money right now before anything changes?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests portability election mechanics and the late-election relief window for a deceased spouse's unused exemption.
scenarios.prompt: My dad died in 2023 with a $6M estate. My mom never filed an estate tax return to elect portability. Is his unused exemption lost forever, or can we still claim it?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests carryover basis on lifetime gifts vs step-up at death, with concrete capital-gains tax math on a house.
scenarios.prompt: My mom bought her house for $90,000 in 1985 and it's worth $750,000 now. If she gifts it to me this year versus I inherit it when she passes, what's the actual tax difference when I sell?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests why selling appreciated assets before death destroys the step-up benefit — a common and costly mistake.
scenarios.prompt: My dad has $400,000 of Apple stock with a $60,000 cost basis, and he's terminally ill. His broker says to sell now to 'lock in the gains.' Is that good advice or a tax disaster?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests annual exclusion per recipient, and gift-splitting with a spouse to double it without touching lifetime exemption.
scenarios.prompt: I want to give my two kids and their spouses $19,000 each this year — $76,000 total. Do I have to file a gift tax return, and does any of this eat into my lifetime exemption?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests the unlimited direct-tuition-payment exclusion: must pay the institution directly, doesn't count as a gift at all.
scenarios.prompt: I paid $45,000 straight to my granddaughter's college for her tuition bill. Does that count against my annual gift exclusion or my lifetime exemption?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests GST tax basics: separate exemption, flat 40% rate above it, and the dynasty-trust concept for skipping a generation.
scenarios.prompt: I have about $10M and want to leave a chunk directly to my grandkids, skipping my kids entirely. What is a generation-skipping trust and what tax hit am I looking at?

scenarios.depth_note: Tests taxation of distributions from an existing GST-exempt trust (DNI to beneficiary) and continued exemption at the beneficiary's death.
scenarios.prompt: My grandmother set up a generation-skipping trust in 2005 that's now worth $8M, and I'm a grandchild receiving distributions. Do I owe income tax on what I receive, and what happens to the trust when I die?
